page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.4-16 is an Arm-based compute instance built on the Ampere AmpereOne processor family operating at a base frequency of 3.0 GHz. The virtual machine allocates 8 dedicated physical cores corresponding to 8 vCPUs with a strict 1.0 thread-per-core topology, ensuring that compute resources are free from the contention and scheduling latency often introduced by simultaneous multithreading. It includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per core.

The hardware configuration features zero onboard local storage, which requires operational disk volumes, persistent databases, and temporary file caches to run across external network-attached block storage. The platform bundles one complimentary public IPv4 address for external network access. There are no discrete GPU accelerators attached, keeping the instance strictly oriented around CPU execution.

With its 1:2 core-to-memory profile, the instance provides cost-effective throughput for compute-oriented tasks without the overhead of unused memory capacity. The dedicated physical core allocation delivers consistent instruction throughput across all cores. The configuration is best aligned with continuous integration pipelines, software build clusters, containerized microservices, API gateways, and native 64-bit Arm development workloads.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A2.Flex.4-16 is a compute-focused instance powered by Ampere AmpereOne processors operating at 3.0 GHz on the arm64 architecture. The server features 8 dedicated physical cores corresponding to 8 vCPUs with one thread per core, backed by 16.0 GB of RAM at a 2.0 GB per core ratio. With no local storage bundled, the instance relies entirely on network-attached block storage for file systems and persistent storage, and it contains no integrated GPU accelerators. Network connectivity includes a single complimentary public IPv4 address. The dedicated core model delivers predictable compute throughput without the resource contention found in multi-threaded configurations. Given its 1:2 core-to-memory ratio, VM.Standard.A2.Flex.4-16 is tailored for Arm-native development, continuous integration pipelines, microservices, container clusters, and distributed worker nodes requiring stable compute capacity.
